method: A disc or tape has exactly two sides, so the planner keeps the running order and chooses one break point in the list. Each side's runtime is the sum of its track durations; every possible break is evaluated and the winner is the one whose longer side is shortest, with a tie going to the smaller difference between the sides. That keeps both sides as near equal as a single break allows, which matters on vinyl because the inner grooves on a long side lose level and high frequencies first. Durations are parsed from the end of each line as minutes:seconds, so 'Night Bus 4:02' and '4:02' both read 242 seconds, and titles are optional. Side limits are conservative nominal capacities for full-level material: 22:00 per side on a 12 in LP at 33⅓ rpm, 12:00 on a 12 in single at 45 rpm, 14:00 on a 10 in LP at 33⅓ rpm, 4:30 on a 7 in single at 45 rpm, 30:00 per side on a C-60 cassette and 45:00 per side on a C-90. The page reports both side totals, the spare time or the amount each side is over, the gap between the sides and the smallest listed medium whose limit covers the longest side. A tracklist that stays inside a medium fits exactly at the limit and one second over it does not. Limits are 2 to 40 tracks and 1 second to 60 minutes per track. The result is a sequencing plan, not a cutting master: vinyl capacity shrinks as level and bass content rise, tape length varies with stock and machine, and track gaps, fades, locked grooves, run-out and lead-in time are not counted. Tracks are never reordered or shortened. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: A 12 in LP at 33⅓ rpm is commonly cut at roughly 18-22 minutes per side, and the usable time falls as level and bass content rise because wider grooves take more space.
Smaller and faster discs hold less: a 12 in single at 45 rpm about 10-15 minutes per side, a 10 in record at 33⅓ rpm about 12-15 minutes, and a 7 in single at 45 rpm about 4-5 minutes.
Compact cassettes are labelled by total playing time for both sides, so a C-60 holds about 30 minutes per side and a C-90 about 45 minutes per side.
Vinyl is cut from the outer edge inward, so a long side ends in the inner grooves where tracing distortion and level loss are greatest; near-equal sides are the usual sequencing target.
